problem: Prior ALFRED methods (Seq2Seq with soft attention over the whole instruction sequence, class-agnostic mask deconvolution, single egocentric view) achieved very low success, especially in unseen scenes (<1-5%).
motivation: ALFRED needs long-horizon reasoning over many step-by-step instructions, a large action space and pixel-level object grounding, and there was a huge gap to human performance. The authors observe that instructions should be processed in order one at a time, that manipulation instructions map almost deterministically to (action, object class) without vision, and that a single narrow view limits navigation.
key_idea: Explicitly select one instruction at a time via a learned COMPLETE token, interpret it in two stages (vision-free action/object-class prediction, then visually grounded), and use multi-view object-centric features with hierarchical attention plus a mask-selection decoder.
insight: Ablations show each part matters: explicit instruction selection lifts val-seen/unseen SR from 2.8/0.5 to 12.9/2.9, the two-stage interpretation adds to 18.9/3.9, and multi-view hierarchical attention reaches 33.7/9.7. Replacing the mask-selection decoder with deconvolution mask prediction collapses SR to 3.8/0.7, showing that selecting among detector masks is critical. Sigmoid gated attention over views beats softmax (33.7 vs 11.9 seen), so views should be merged rather than selected. More views help (1 view 18.9, 3 views 25.9, 5 views 33.7 seen).
method: Object-centric visual features: a Mask R-CNN (ResNet-50, 300x300 input, N=32 detections) provides per-object features, masks and confidence scores for each of K=5 egocentric views (center, up/down ±15°, left/right ±90°).

Instruction selection: a virtual COMPLETE action is added to each instruction's action sequence; when the action decoder predicts it, the instruction index m_t increments, so only one instruction encoding s_{m_t} is used at each step.

Instruction decoder (stage 1): two LSTMs reset to s_{m_t} predict, without vision, the action and object-class sequences (p^ia, p^io), trained with the auxiliary loss L_aux. Navigation targets are collapsed to minimal sequences with None objects, and learnable constant vectors are fed downstream for navigation.

Action decoder (stage 2): hierarchical attention (per-view soft attention over objects conditioned on s_{m_t}, weighted by confidence, then sigmoid gated attention across views) gives v_t. An LSTM initialized with the goal-statement encoding takes [v_t; s_{m_t}; p^ia; p^io] and outputs actions including COMPLETE.

Mask decoder: single-head light-weight self-attention over the center-view object features, then a bilinear score with [s; p^ia; p^io] selects one of the N detected masks; trained with BCE against the highest-IoU match.
Training: imitation learning on expert demonstrations, L = L_mask + L_action + L_aux; Adam lr 1e-3 halved at epochs 5/8/10, batch size 32, 15 epochs; Mask R-CNN pretrained on 800K replayed frames.
Ensemble (challenge entry): 4 models with different seeds and mask-decoder variants share one detector and average action and object probabilities.

setting.backbone: Mask R-CNN (ResNet-50) + GloVe/LSTM encoders and decoders with attention (trained from scratch, imitation learning)
setting.training_data: ALFRED expert demonstrations (8,055 episodes / 25,743 language directives, train split); Mask R-CNN trained on 800K frames with instance masks from replayed training demonstrations
setting.observation: egocentric RGB from 5 views (center, up, down, left, right) converted to object-centric features; single-view variant uses RGB center only
setting.action_space: 12 discrete ALFRED actions (5 navigation e.g. MoveAhead/RotateRight, 7 manipulation e.g. Pickup/ToggleOn) plus COMPLETE token, with a selected object instance mask for manipulation
setting.privileged: none (uses expert instruction-to-action alignment only at training time)

numbers_note: ALFRED is not in the canonical benchmark list, so it is labelled 'ALFRED'; keys SR/GC are Task and Goal-Cond success, PLW* are path-length-weighted versions. Test-seen and val results for the single-view and ensemble variants are also in the paper but only main rows are listed.
results: The 5-view model reaches 8.37% task SR on test-unseen and 29.16% on test-seen, versus the previously published SOTA of 0.39%/3.98% (Shridhar et al.) and the concurrent MOCA at 5.30%/22.05%. Even the single-view model (4.45% unseen) beats all published baselines except MOCA on seen. An ensemble gives 9.42% unseen.
limitations: Navigation remains the bottleneck (Goto sub-goal only 59% seen / 39% unseen); failures come from ambiguous instructions, wrong position for the next manipulation, and walking into obstacles.

Multi-view input is slow because AI2-THOR cannot render multiple views directly (the agent must rotate to capture them), and ensembling multiplies compute; the detector misses small or unseen objects.
Absolute success in unseen scenes stays very low (8.37%) versus 91% for humans.
